Row & Column Swaps

InvariantsLogic

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)

Game: Swap rows and columns of the grid. For N=3, try to match the target — it cannot be done.
How to play: Press a row or column arrow, then another arrow of the same kind to swap them.

Your grid

Target (unreachable)

Look for the math

Swapping rows and columns feels like it reshuffles everything, yet a simple invariant shows why some patterns can never appear.

Columns are bags

Start with numbers 1 … N² written in order across each row. For N = 3 the columns are the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, {3,6,9}. A column swap only moves whole bags around. A row swap reorders numbers inside every bag but never changes which numbers share a column.

The target breaks the bags

The olympiad target flips the middle row to 6 5 4, so the columns become {1,6,7}, {2,5,8}, {3,4,9} — not a rearrangement of the three bags. The logic test checks that every sequence of swaps keeps the column sets, that the target’s sets differ, and that a full search of the (3!)² = 36 reachable grids never hits the target. (The original applet’s Reset filled the grid column-major; this port follows the page’s olympiad left pattern instead.)

Rows tell the same story

The same argument works with rows as bags. Either view is enough: if a pattern’s row sets or column sets are wrong, no amount of swapping will produce it.

With N=3, swap freely and watch which numbers stay together in a column. Then look at the target’s middle column — a stranger has joined the bag.
